quiz.question_id: Manakah operasi yang aman ketika `var p *int` masih nil?
quiz.question_en: Which operation is safe when `var p *int` is still nil?
options_id: `fmt.Println(*p)`
`fmt.Println(p == nil)`
`fmt.Println((*p) + 1)`
options_en: `fmt.Println(*p)`
`fmt.Println(p == nil)`
`fmt.Println((*p) + 1)`

quiz.question_id: Mengapa deklarasi pointer tanpa inisialisasi sendiri tidak panic?
quiz.question_en: Why does declaring an uninitialized pointer by itself not panic?
options_id: Karena panic hanya terjadi saat pointer nil benar-benar didereference atau field-nya diakses
Karena compiler diam-diam mengalokasikan memori target
Karena semua pointer nil otomatis menjadi pointer ke zero value
Karena nil pointer hanya berbahaya di method receiver
options_en: Because a panic only happens when a nil pointer is actually dereferenced or one of its fields is accessed
Because the compiler silently allocates the target memory
Because all nil pointers automatically become pointers to zero values
Because nil pointers are only dangerous in method receivers

quiz.question_id: Apa pola idiomatis setelah `user := findUser(id)` ketika fungsi bisa mengembalikan nil?
quiz.question_en: What is the idiomatic pattern after `user := findUser(id)` when the function may return nil?
options_id: Langsung akses `user.Name` lalu recover jika panic
Cek `if user == nil` lalu tangani kondisi tidak ditemukan lebih awal
Bandingkan `user` dengan struct kosong
Ubah `user` menjadi interface kosong lebih dulu
options_en: Access `user.Name` immediately and recover if it panics
Check `if user == nil` and handle the not-found case early
Compare `user` with an empty struct
Convert `user` to an empty interface first

quiz.question_en: Why does `var a Animal = (*Dog)(nil)` make `a != nil`?
options_id: Karena interface menyimpan pasangan tipe dan nilai; tipenya terisi walaupun nilai pointer di dalamnya nil
Karena interface tidak pernah bisa bernilai nil
Karena pointer nil otomatis dikonversi menjadi error
Karena `Dog` bukan struct
options_en: Because an interface stores a type-and-value pair; the type is present even though the pointer value inside is nil
Because an interface can never be nil
Because nil pointers are automatically converted to errors
Because `Dog` is not a struct

quiz.question_id: Mengapa pemeriksaan `a == nil` tidak cukup untuk interface yang mungkin menyimpan typed nil pointer?
quiz.question_en: Why is checking `a == nil` not enough for an interface that may store a typed nil pointer?
options_id: Karena operator `==` tidak valid untuk interface
Karena interface bisa non-nil walaupun nilai konkret di dalamnya nil
Karena semua interface selalu berisi zero value struct
Karena type assertion tidak bekerja pada interface nil
options_en: Because the `==` operator is not valid for interfaces
Because an interface can be non-nil even when the concrete value inside it is nil
Because every interface always contains a zero-value struct
Because type assertions do not work on nil interfaces

quiz.question_id: Mengapa method nil-safe seperti `func (n *Node) Length() int` berguna?
quiz.question_en: Why are nil-safe methods like `func (n *Node) Length() int` useful?
options_id: Karena method receiver pointer tidak pernah bisa nil
Karena mereka memungkinkan struktur rekursif diperlakukan aman bahkan saat receiver nil
Karena semua method di Go wajib return int saat receiver nil
Karena mereka menghilangkan kebutuhan unit test
options_en: Because pointer method receivers can never be nil
Because they let recursive structures be handled safely even when the receiver is nil
Because all Go methods must return int when the receiver is nil
Because they eliminate the need for unit tests

quiz.question_id: Apa tujuan helper seperti `derefInt(p *int, def int)`?
quiz.question_en: What is the purpose of helpers like `derefInt(p *int, def int)`?
options_id: Mengubah pointer menjadi interface
Memberi nilai default ketika pointer nil tanpa menyebabkan panic
Memaksa semua pointer dialokasikan di heap
Mengganti semua pointer dengan zero value
options_en: To turn pointers into interfaces
To provide a default when a pointer is nil without causing a panic
To force all pointers onto the heap
To replace all pointers with zero values

quiz.question_id: Dalam desain API, kapan pointer nil sering dipakai secara sah?
quiz.question_en: In API design, when is a nil pointer often used legitimately?
options_id: Sebagai penanda nilai opsional atau tidak ada data
Sebagai pengganti semua boolean
Untuk menghindari return error
Untuk membuat interface selalu nil
options_en: As a marker for an optional value or missing data
As a replacement for all booleans
To avoid returning errors
To make interfaces always nil

quiz.question_id: Apa trade-off dari menggunakan pointer untuk optional field seperti `Bio *string`?
quiz.question_en: What is the trade-off of using a pointer for an optional field like `Bio *string`?
options_id: Kita bisa membedakan 'belum diset' dari nilai string biasa, tetapi caller perlu menangani kemungkinan nil
Field menjadi selalu aman didereference tanpa cek
String tidak lagi comparable
Pointer menghilangkan kebutuhan zero value
options_en: We can distinguish 'not set yet' from an ordinary string value, but callers must handle the possibility of nil
The field becomes always safe to dereference without checks
Strings are no longer comparable
Pointers eliminate the need for zero values

quiz.question_id: Pernyataan mana yang paling tepat tentang safe access di Go?
quiz.question_en: Which statement is most accurate about safe access in Go?
options_id: Safe access berarti menunggu panic lalu memakai recover di semua fungsi
Safe access berarti mendesain alur kode agar nil diperiksa atau ditangani sebelum dereference terjadi
Safe access berarti menghindari semua pointer
Safe access hanya relevan untuk interface, bukan pointer
options_en: Safe access means waiting for a panic and then using recover in every function
Safe access means designing code so nil is checked or handled before dereferencing occurs
Safe access means avoiding all pointers
Safe access is only relevant to interfaces, not pointers
